profile.name: Suhaas Vellanki
profile.title: Aspiring AI Engineer
profile.intro: I build practical AI systems and data-driven tools that turn messy information into dependable decisions. My work sits at the intersection of machine learning, automation, and product thinking, with a focus on helping teams move from raw signals to useful action.

paragraphs: I am an AI engineering student with a leaning toward applied machine learning, intelligent automation, and data-driven problem solving. I enjoy building systems that are useful in the real world, not just accurate in a notebook.

My engineering mindset is shaped by mountaineering: steady pacing, reading the terrain before committing, and preparing thoroughly so the climb stays manageable. I like to move deliberately, validate assumptions, and make small improvements that compound over time.

experience._comment: Primary experience appears in the main timeline.
bullets: Migrated statistical forecasting pipelines of 30+ training, testing, and validation notebooks from Databricks to Snowflake, driving consolidation of ML workflows onto a single enterprise platform.
Designed and deployed an automated pricing data-collection algorithm that analyzes pricing for thousands of electronic parts daily, now in production and used by the Pricing team.
Expanded on my product pricing data collection system by developing a prediction algorithm that analyzes variations in pricing data.
Developed an automated transaction-cleaning system that detects and reprocesses stuck Oracle WMS transactions, enhancing operational efficiency for the Supply Chain team.
Engineered several other intelligent automation solutions for Supply Chain, Pricing, and Finance teams, leveraging data integration and workflow orchestration to improve operational efficiencies.
Led AI initiatives at an early-stage startup, designing and implementing end-to-end production AI pipelines.
Implemented intent-classification models to accurately route chatbot queries and improve conversational flow.
Built privacy-aware data-parsing capabilities to safeguard sensitive user information and ensure compliant data handling.
Developed secure data pull/push mechanisms that enable the agent to interact with internal systems and execute workflow actions.

Supported development of AI-driven healthcare applications, including a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system enabling medical professionals to query large libraries of research papers, journals, and clinical manuals through a conversational interface.
Also worked in project-based capacity under direct guidance of one of the senior supervisors, where I worked on a RAG model and a Sentiment Analysis Classification Model.
Taught 2D Game Design in Scratch, Python, HTML/CSS, JavaScript, Lua, and C to K-12 students in the format of both 2-on-1 sessions and lecture classes.
Mentored Middle and High School students with more advanced projects, such as hackathon submissions, passion projects, and personal websites.
Taught computer science skills to K-12 students such as block-based coding, game design, and basic programming with Python and Java.
Taught online Fall classes to Pakistani orphans.
Maintained User Interfaces, improved backend systems and worked on data collection with Python programming.
Researched, collected data and developed ML models for redshift prediction using Random Forest Regression.
Wrote a research paper where I used machine learning to estimate photometric redshift from infrared data from the James Webb Space Telescope.

fieldNotes.name: Kilimanjaro Summit
fieldNotes.summary: “Pole pole” taught me that sustained effort beats speed when the route is long and the air is thin.
fieldNotes.title: Kilimanjaro
fieldNotes.content: It is easy to mistake effort for progress when everything is moving quickly. On Kilimanjaro, the lesson was the opposite: a disciplined pace matters more than a dramatic burst. The route became a reminder that making steady progress under pressure is often the most reliable way to reach a difficult goal.

fieldNotes.name: Tour du Mont Blanc
fieldNotes.summary: Linking valleys, passes, and borders into one continuous route felt like systems integration at altitude.
fieldNotes.title: Tour du Mont Blanc
fieldNotes.content: The route links many valleys, passes, and borders into one continuous movement. It felt like a live map of how systems fit together: each section depended on the one before it, and each change in terrain affected the next decision.

fieldNotes.name: Everest Base Camp
fieldNotes.summary: Acclimatization, iteration, and respecting limits made the route feel like an engineering sprint with guardrails.
fieldNotes.title: Everest Base Camp
fieldNotes.content: Altitude changes the way you think. It reduces confidence in bold assumptions and asks instead for humility, repetition, and respect for the environment. Every stage on the route had a reason behind it, and the best decisions were not the fastest ones but the ones that kept the whole plan viable.

fieldNotes.name: Balkan Peaks Trail
fieldNotes.summary: When the route is uncertain, good judgment matters more than perfect information.
fieldNotes.title: Balkan Peaks Trail
fieldNotes.content: Some routes are not perfectly mapped, and some decisions have to be made with incomplete information. That is a familiar feeling in engineering work too: not every dataset is clean, not every signal is complete, and not every assumption can be validated before the next step.
